content.text:
My family
Rappelle-toi / Recall:
What do je, il and elle mean?
Say 12, 13 and 14 in French.
Identify family members using mon père, ma mère, mon frère, ma sœur, mes parents and mes grands-parents, choosing mon, ma or mes to match the French noun.
Describe a family member’s name, age and one personality trait using il/elle s’appelle…, il/elle a… ans and il/elle est…, with correct agreement of gentil/gentille and amusant/amusante.
Write a short description of your own or an imaginary family using j’ai… and je n’ai pas de… to describe siblings, followed by details about one family member’s name, age and personality.

elements.name: Diagram
elements.alt: Three learning objectives for describing family members.

slides.notes:
Running
Take about 1 minute to introduce the learning goals. Pupils read them silently, then name one thing they already know about describing family in French.

Background
These objectives bring together family vocabulary, adjective agreement and a short piece of connected writing.

content.text: Écoute et répète / Listen and repeat

elements.name: Diagram
elements.alt: A central teenage speaker is surrounded by six family panels; the parents and grandparents panels each show two people.

slides.notes:
Running
Spend about 5 minutes listening and repeating together. Read aloud: « moi, mon père, ma mère, mon frère, ma sœur, mes parents, mes grands-parents ». Pause after each phrase for pupils to repeat, then repeat the sequence once more.

Misconceptions
Pupils may choose mon or ma according to whether the speaker is a boy or a girl. The French noun decides: say mon père and ma mère, whoever is speaking.

Background
French possessive adjectives agree with the noun that follows, not with the person who owns it. Mes is used before plural nouns.

content.text: The French noun decides (not the person speaking.)

slides.notes:
Running
Allow about 4 minutes for pupils to say or write the matching phrases individually. Check the six answers as a class and ask pupils to explain why the possessive changes.

Answers
1. mon père
2. ma mère
3. mon frère
4. ma sœur
5. mes parents
6. mes grands-parents

Misconceptions
Pupils may use mon for every male family member and ma for every female one. These words match the French noun: père and frère are masculine; mère and sœur are feminine; parents and grands-parents are plural, so use mes.

Background
Père and mère are the singular words for father and mother. Parents and grands-parents are plural forms.

content.text: A girl says: « ___ père, ___ mère, ___ parents ». Which set fits?

slides.notes:
Running
Give pupils about 3 minutes to choose an option alone, then compare with a partner. Take a class vote and ask a pupil to justify the answer using each noun.

Answers
C — mon, ma, mes

Misconceptions
A uses mon for parents, but parents is plural and needs mes. B uses ma for père, but père is masculine. D uses mon for mère, but mère is feminine. The correct sequence is mon père, ma mère, mes parents.

Background
The speaker being a girl does not change the possessive adjective. The noun determines whether to use mon, ma or mes.

content.text: Il / elle = he / she. In French, age uses a: ‘has’.
Mon frère s’appelle Léo. Il a treize ans. Il est gentil et amusant.
Ma sœur s’appelle Léa. Elle a treize ans. Elle est gentille et amusante.

elements.name: Photo
elements.alt: A friendly teenage brother and sister stand together, both smiling.
elements.request: Two friendly teenage siblings, a boy and a girl. teenage boy. teenage girl. friendly smiles

slides.notes:
Running
Spend about 5 minutes reading the two examples aloud. Pupils identify the name, age and personality detail in each, then practise reading one sentence each with a partner.

Misconceptions
Pupils may use être for age, as in English, or give the adjective the wrong ending. In French, age uses avoir: il a treize ans. Match the adjective to the person: gentil and amusant for a boy; gentille and amusante for a girl.

Background
S’appeler means ‘to be called’. French uses avoir, literally ‘to have’, to state someone’s age. Many adjectives add -e in the feminine form.

content.text: Brother: Hugo, 14, kind. Write three sentences: name, age and personality.
Sister: Inès, 12, funny. Write three sentences: name, age and personality.

Écris en français / Write in French.
Name: s’appelle • Age: a … ans • Personality: est
kind: gentil/gentille • funny: amusant/amusante
12: douze • 14: quatorze

slides.notes:
Running
Give pupils about 7 minutes to write the two descriptions independently. Ask them to underline the name, age and personality phrase, then check the adjective endings with a partner.

Answers
1. Mon frère s’appelle Hugo. Il a quatorze ans. Il est gentil.
2. Ma sœur s’appelle Inès. Elle a douze ans. Elle est amusante.

Misconceptions
Pupils may write il for the sister or elle for the brother; link il to Hugo and elle to Inès. They may also leave the adjective unchanged: use gentil for Hugo and amusante for Inès. Say il a / elle a for age, not il est / elle est.

Background
Quatorze and douze are the French words for 14 and 12. The adjective endings here match the gender of the person described.

content.text: J’ai = I have. Je n’ai pas de = I don’t have any.
J’ai un frère et deux sœurs. / I have a brother and two sisters.
Je n’ai pas de frère. / I don’t have any brothers.

elements.name: Diagram
elements.alt: J’ai un frère becomes je n’ai pas de frère; j’ai une sœur becomes je n’ai pas de sœur.

slides.notes:
Running
Spend about 5 minutes reading the examples together. Pupils make one affirmative and one negative sentence about siblings, using the sentence pattern shown.

Misconceptions
Pupils may keep un or une after the negative, or omit de. In this construction, say je n’ai pas de frère and je n’ai pas de sœur. With an affirmative sentence, use un or une: j’ai un frère; j’ai une sœur.

Background
In French, the article usually changes to de after ne… pas when saying you do not have something. The phrase is pronounced as one unit: je n’ai pas de.

content.text: Un petit texte / A short text
J’ai une sœur. Je n’ai pas de frère.
Ma sœur s’appelle Zoé. Elle a douze ans.

elements.name: Photo
elements.alt: A teenage girl and her younger sister, together with both smiling faces clearly visible.
elements.request: A teenage speaker with one younger sister. teenage speaker. younger sister. two smiling faces

slides.notes:
Running
Allow about 4 minutes for pupils to read the short text aloud in pairs. Ask them to identify its sibling sentences and the three details about the sister.

Misconceptions
Pupils may write une after the negative, or use elle est for age. Keep de in je n’ai pas de frère, and use elle a douze ans for age. Gentille and amusante describe a feminine person.

Background
The text combines the negative sibling structure with the name, age and personality patterns practised earlier. Zoé is a feminine name, so the example uses elle and feminine adjective forms.

content.text: Décris ta famille / Describe your family
You have one brother and no sisters. Write both sibling sentences.
Your brother is called Sami. He is 13 and kind. Add his name, age and personality.

Écris un petit texte / Write a short text.
13 = treize • kind = gentil/gentille

slides.notes:
Running
Give pupils about 8 minutes to write the sibling sentences and description independently. Have them check the pronoun, age verb and adjective ending before sharing with a partner.

Answers
J’ai un frère. Je n’ai pas de sœur. Mon frère s’appelle Sami. Il a treize ans. Il est gentil.

Misconceptions
Pupils may use je n’ai pas une sœur; after this negative use de: je n’ai pas de sœur. They may use elle for Sami or write est treize ans. Use il for Sami and il a treize ans for his age.

Background
Treize means 13. Sami is a boy’s name in this example, so the description uses il and the masculine form gentil.

content.text: Write about your own or an imaginary family: say which siblings you have and one sibling type you do not have.
Describe one family member: name, age and one personality trait.
Check mon/ma/mes, il/elle, a … ans and the adjective ending.

Écris 5–6 phrases / Write 5–6 sentences.
Help: j’ai • je n’ai pas de • s’appelle • a • est
kind: gentil/gentille • funny: amusant/amusante
Stretch: describe a second family member with a different pronoun.

slides.notes:
Running
Allow about 12 minutes for pupils to write 5–6 sentences independently. They should include a sibling they have, one sibling type they do not have, and name, age and personality details for one family member. Invite confident pupils to complete the stretch by describing another person with a different pronoun.

Answers
Example: J’ai un frère. Je n’ai pas de sœur. Mon frère s’appelle Adam. Il a douze ans. Il est gentil.

Misconceptions
Pupils may use the wrong possessive for the family noun, mismatch il or elle, use être for age, or forget the feminine adjective ending. Check that the possessive matches the noun, the pronoun matches the person, age uses a, and the adjective agrees: for example, ma sœur… elle est gentille.

Background
A short connected description can be built from familiar sentence patterns. Encourage pupils to use an imaginary family if they prefer not to write about their own.
